newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam Airlines sees sharp decline in growth.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam Airlines sees sharp decline in growth.

text.p: Vietnam's national carrier, Vietnam Airlines, said on Friday its growth rate during the first seven months of this year had fallen sharply and blamed a slowdown in the economy.

An airline official told Reuters that growth between 1993 and 1995 had reached an annual rate of 35 percent, but said that in the first seven months of this year the level had fallen to just eight percent.

The official, who declined to be identified, said 1,591,306 passengers travelled with the airline during the period, of which 978,500 were domestic passengers. The airline also carried some 24,700 tonnes of cargo.
Comparative figure for the numbers carried in 1996 were not available.

The official gave a range of reasons for the decline, including the political crisis in neighbouring Cambodia, competition from regional airlines, and diversification among passengers towards other forms of transport.

But the semi-official Dau Tu newspaper quoted Luong Hoai Nam of the airline's marketing and planning department as saying falling confidence in Vietnam among foreign investors, declining tourist interest and lowered consumer spending were also causes.
Vietnam's economy has continued to boom, but this year has seen signs of the first slowdown since free-market reforms were launched in the late 1980s.

The Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper reported this week that the number of foreign investment projects licensed this year has fallen by 23 and 35 percent against 1996 and 1995, although officials say the quality of investment has improved.

Tourist arrivals are also down. The Vietnam Airlines official said interest in travel to Vietnam in Europe and the United States had remained steady so far this year, but travellers in Asia were showing less interest.

The National Administration of Tourism said in June that 700,000 foreigners visited Vietnam in the first six months of this year, representing a seven percent decline compared to the same period in 1996.
